title: Microlithic Quartz Stone Tool Artifacts
summary: Archaeological evidence at Kamabai and Yengema rock shelters proves early human hunter-gatherer occupation in Sierra Leone.

title: Iron Age Metallurgy & Early Agricultural Societies
summary: Development of ironworking, oil palm cultivation, and rice agriculture among early coastal and interior societies.

title: Pedro de Sintra Names 'Serra Leoa'
summary: Portuguese explorer Pedro de Sintra charts the mountainous peninsula and names it Serra Leoa (Lion Mountains).

title: Establishment of Bunce Island Slave Castle
summary: English trading companies construct Bunce Island fort in the Sierra Leone River as a major center for transatlantic captive export.

title: Founding of Granville Town (Black Poor)
summary: Abolitionists help settle over 400 Black Poor from London at Granville Town on land purchased from King Naimbana.

title: Arrival of Nova Scotian Settlers & Founding of Freetown
summary: 1,196 Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia land under Thomas Peters and John Clarkson, naming the settlement Freetown.

title: Arrival of Jamaican Maroons
summary: Over 500 Jamaican Maroons arrive in Freetown following their uprising in Trelawny Town, helping defend the colony.

title: Freetown Becomes a British Crown Colony
summary: The British Crown assumes direct control of Freetown from the Sierra Leone Company and establishes the Vice-Admiralty Court.

title: Founding of Fourah Bay College
summary: Church Missionary Society establishes Fourah Bay College, the first Western-style university institution in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Declaration of British Protectorate
summary: Britain unilaterally declares a Protectorate over the interior hinterland without consultation with indigenous paramount chiefs.

title: Hut Tax War Led by Bai Bureh
summary: Paramount Chief Bai Bureh leads anti-colonial armed resistance against the British taxation policy across northern and southern districts.

title: Discovery of Diamonds in Kono District
summary: Geological survey discovers rich alluvial diamond deposits in Kono, transforming Sierra Leone's economic and political destiny.

title: Formation of Sierra Leone People's Party (SLPP)
summary: Dr. Milton Margai leads the formation of the SLPP, uniting protectorate chiefs and elites toward self-governance.

title: Independence of Sierra Leone
summary: On 27 April 1961, Sierra Leone gains independence from Great Britain with Sir Milton Margai as its first Prime Minister.

title: APC Election Victory & First Military Coup
summary: Siaka Stevens' APC wins democratic elections; Brigadier David Lansana initiates military intervention, leading to NRC rule.

title: Establishment of One-Party APC State
summary: President Siaka Stevens enacts a new constitution establishing single-party rule under the All People's Congress.

title: Outbreak of Sierra Leone Civil War
summary: Revolutionary United Front (RUF) led by Foday Sankoh crosses from Liberia into Bomaru, initiating an 11-year conflict.

title: NPRC Military Coup Led by Valentine Strasser
summary: Junior officers overthrow President Joseph Saidu Momoh and form the National Provisional Ruling Council (NPRC).

title: Democratic Multi-Party Elections & President Kabbah
summary: Ahmad Tejan Kabbah of the SLPP wins restored multi-party elections amidst ongoing civil conflict.

title: Lomé Peace Agreement
summary: Government of Sierra Leone and RUF sign peace accord in Lomé, Togo, paving way for UNAMSIL deployment.

title: Official End of Civil War & Declaration of Peace
summary: President Kabbah declares civil war officially ended; disarmament of over 75,000 fighters completed; TRC established.

title: Special Court for Sierra Leone Begins Trials
summary: UN-backed tribunal opens in Freetown to try individuals bearing greatest responsibility for war crimes and crimes against humanity.

title: Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak
summary: Ebola epidemic spreads across West Africa; Sierra Leone records nearly 14,000 cases before being declared Ebola-free in 2016.

title: Regent Landslide Disaster
summary: Catastrophic mudslide at Mount Sugar Loaf in Regent kills over 1,000 residents and highlights climate vulnerability.

title: Presidential Election of Julius Maada Bio
summary: Julius Maada Bio (SLPP) wins presidential election, launching the flagship Free Quality School Education policy.

title: General Elections & Ongoing Democratic Governance
summary: Presidential elections conducted with President Bio re-elected; cross-party dialogue mediated by ECOWAS and Commonwealth.
